CrystallineCohomology.summary: The libraries supply the elementary divided-power algebra this roadmap starts from and nothing above it. Mathlib has the full `DividedPowers` structure on an ideal, PD morphisms, sub-PD ideals and PD quotients, the x^n/n! structure on ℚ-algebras and on invertible-factorial ideals, the canonical divided powers on (p) ⊆ ℤ_p for every prime including p = 2, and the universal divided power algebra Γ_R(M) with its (weak) lifting property; it also has Witt vectors with Frobenius/Verschiebung/Teichmüller/ghost components, W(k) as a complete DVR, F-isocrystals with the one-dimensional Dieudonné–Manin classification, and Fontaine's θ : W(R♭) → R with its surjectivity (so A_inf and θ, which CR.0 exports, already exist). Everything genuinely crystalline is missing: there is no PD envelope at all (not even the PD structure on Γ_R(M) — mathlib's own TODO), no algebraic de Rham complex Ω^•, no connections or stratifications on modules, no crystalline site, no crystals, no de Rham–Witt or Dieudonné complexes, no A_cris, no logarithmic structures, no Hyodo–Kato theory, no Dieudonné crystals, and no cup product/Künneth/trace formalism in sheaf cohomology. CR.0 is therefore partly built and every later layer is not built; CR.7 is an export/interface layer.

targets.target: Divided power structure (A, I, γ) on an ideal with the full axiom list (dpow_add, dpow_mul, dpow_comp, n!·γ_n(x) = x^n, nilpotence of elements of a PD ideal)
targets.note: Over a CommSemiring, no nilpotence or completeness hypothesis; `grep -n sorry` on Mathlib/RingTheory/DividedPowers/ and DividedPowerAlgebra/ returns nothing. The zero-ideal acceptance example is `dividedPowersBot`.

targets.target: PD morphisms, their composition, generation-by-generators criterion and functoriality
targets.note: Both bundled and unbundled forms, with the `on_span` reduction used for checking PD compatibility on generators. This is the 'PD morphism' the layer wants to base-change.

targets.target: The formula γ_n(x) = x^n/n! as a construction over torsionfree/rational bases, its uniqueness, and the ways it fails in a torsion ring
targets.note: `OfInvertibleFactorial.dividedPowers` needs only (n-1)! invertible and I^n = 0, so it is strictly more general than the ℚ-algebra case; `dividedPowers_unique` is the uniqueness the layer asks for. The torsion-ring failure case is exactly what these hypotheses exclude, but no counterexample declaration exists.

targets.target: The canonical p-PD ideal: divided powers on (p) ⊆ ℤ_p, treating p = 2 explicitly
targets.note: Hypothesis is only `[Fact p.Prime]`, so p = 2 is covered with no separate argument (the construction descends x^n/n! from ℚ_p along the injection ℤ_p → ℚ_p). The file's TODO notes the open ramified generalisation (π) ⊆ R for e ≤ p−1, which the layer does not request.

targets.target: Sub-PD ideals, PD quotients, dp equalizers and the kernel/image of a PD morphism
targets.note: The sub-PD ideals form a complete lattice and `SubDPIdeal.span` computes the sub-PD ideal generated by a set. These are exactly the tools the PD-envelope construction of Berthelot–Ogus §3 is built from, which is why the layer calls its work 'extending the existing PD API'.

targets.target: PD polynomial algebra / universal divided power algebra Γ_A(M) over a fixed PD base, with its own PD structure and the full universal property
targets.note: Missing: the canonical divided power structure on the augmentation ideal of Γ_R(M) — the file's own TODO reads 'Show in upcoming files that DividedPowerAlgebra R M has divided powers', and only a *weak* universal property (lifting to a ring already carrying divided powers) is proved. Base-compatibility over a PD base (A,I,γ) and a free/finite-variable PD polynomial algebra A⟨x_1,…,x_n⟩ with its PD ideal are also absent.

targets.target: The PD envelope D_{B,γ}(J) of an ideal J in an A-algebra over a PD base: existence as initial object, functorial morphisms, universality
targets.note: No declaration or docstring in either library mentions an envelope of a PD structure: `grep -rn -i envelope` over Mathlib/RingTheory/DividedPower*/ and TauCeti/TauCeti/RingTheory/DividedPowers/ is empty, and the only `*Envelope*` names in the baseline are injective envelopes of modules, Gaussian/Chebyshev envelopes and triangulated envelopes.

targets.target: Base change, localization and transitivity of PD envelopes under their actual hypotheses
targets.note: Depends on the envelope itself; nothing exists. Mathlib has the generic localization/base-change machinery (`IsLocalization`, `Algebra.TensorProduct`) but no PD-compatible statement.

targets.target: Explicit PD envelope of a polynomial regular immersion, and comparison with the derived PD construction in the lci range
targets.note: Absent; the derived PD functor it must be compared with is itself a DD.0 target that is also absent (no derived symmetric/divided power functors in either library).

targets.target: p-completed PD envelopes, with the boundedness/torsion conditions that let ordinary completion replace derived completion
targets.note: Only ordinary I-adic completion exists (with exactness and flatness lemmas); derived completeness, which is what the comparison is about, is not defined anywhere (no `IsDerivedComplete`, no derived Koszul completion).

targets.target: PD nilpotence and the PD filtration I^{[n]}, kept separate from ordinary ideal nilpotence and from nilpotence of p
targets.note: Mathlib proves elements of a PD ideal of a ℚ-free ring are nilpotent, and has the sub-PD ideal generated by a set, but there is no PD-filtration definition I^{[n]} and no `IsPDNilpotent` predicate, so the three conditions the layer insists on distinguishing are not even nameable yet.

targets.target: A_inf = W(R♭) and θ : A_inf → R, with the Witt reduction map and surjectivity
targets.note: θ is built for any CommRing R with `[Fact ¬IsUnit (p : R)]` and `[IsAdicComplete (span {p}) R]` — i.e. an integral-perfectoid-style hypothesis package, which covers O_C. The layer exports this object; AInfCohomology AI.0 also claims ownership of it, so the two should not both build it.

targets.target: A_cris: the p-completed PD envelope of ker(θ : A_inf → O_C), and the maps induced by Witt reduction and θ
targets.note: Mathlib builds B_dR^+ as the ker(θ[1/p])-adic completion of W(R♭)[1/p] and B_dR by inverting a generator, but nothing PD: no A_cris, no B_cris. `grep -i -P '\t[^\t]*(Acris|A_cris|cris\b)'` on declarations.tsv is empty. Note also that BDeRham.lean's own TODO records that principality of ker θ is not yet proved, so its generator-inverting definition is provisional.

duplicates.note: Builds prismatic envelopes by δ-adjunction plus derived completion and explicitly says 'Compare with the PD envelopes already built in CR.0', so the two envelope constructions share the universal-property/flatness/regularity work but PR.0 defers the PD case to here.

Constructs A_inf = W(O_C^♭), its Frobenius and θ, and states 'A_cris is the completed PD envelope from CR.0' — the A_inf/θ/A_cris targets of CR.0 are the same objects, with AI.0 owning the ξ/μ normalisation and CR.0 the envelope.
Imports 'generic PD envelopes from CrystallineCohomology CR.0' and the shared A_inf/θ to build B_dR, B_cris and B_st; same period-ring objects, downstream of this layer.
Identifies the p-completed derived de Rham description of A_cris and needs the explicit maps to the PD period rings supplied by CR.0/AI.0; overlapping A_cris target from the derived side.

Constructs homogeneous degree-n polynomial laws 'representing divided powers and their tensor/base-change maps' — that is Roby's representing algebra Γ, the same object as CR.0's PD polynomial algebra, approached through polynomial laws.

targets.target: Small and big crystalline sites with objects (U, T, δ) and PD closed immersions U → T over a PD base, with the p-locally-nilpotent convention and Zariski/étale covering topology
targets.note: Generic site machinery (Grothendieck topologies, coverages, pretopologies, the small Zariski and étale sites of a scheme) is in mathlib, but the crystalline site itself does not exist: `grep -i -P '\t[^\t]*Crystalline'` on declarations.tsv returns zero rows in both libraries, and `grep -rn -i crystalline` in the Lean trees finds only bibliography entries in the DividedPowers files.

targets.target: Morphisms to the underlying scheme site, structure sheaf O_{X/S} and PD-ideal sheaf on the crystalline site, and comparison between the site variants
targets.note: Nothing crystalline exists; the underlying tools (continuous functors of sites, `Sites/Continuous.lean`, induced topologies, sheaves of modules on a site) are present in mathlib but not instantiated.

targets.target: Crystals in quasi-coherent modules, finite locally free crystals, isocrystals, F-crystals, with tensor/duality and exact structures
targets.note: Mathlib's `Isocrystal` is a K(p,k)-vector space with a φ-semilinear automorphism over a perfect domain k — precisely the 'bare semilinear vector space' the layer warns against identifying with an isocrystal on a site. There is no crystal (no site to live on), no quasi-coherent-crystal category, no tensor/duality on crystals.

targets.target: Evaluation of a crystal on a lift, PD stratifications, and the equivalence with integrable quasi-nilpotent connections over a formally smooth lift
targets.note: Ω¹_{B/A} and derivations exist, but there is no notion of a connection ∇ : M → M ⊗ Ω¹ on a module over a ring, hence no integrability, no quasi-nilpotence, and no stratification: `grep -i -P '\t[^\t]*Stratification'` is empty and every `Connection` hit is either a Galois connection or a Levi-Civita connection on a smooth vector bundle.

targets.target: Taylor expansion and cocycle identities for a PD stratification
targets.note: Absent for the same reason; mathlib's `taylor`/`Polynomial.taylor` is the polynomial shift operator and is unrelated.

duplicates.note: Constructs the logarithmic crystalline site and crystals with log connections — the same site/crystal constructions with a log structure added.
Owns q-differentials and coordinate comparisons against the crystalline-site picture; overlapping connection/stratification formalism in the q-deformed setting.
q-crystalline charts and the AΩ comparison reuse the crystalline-site/stratification comparison in the q-crystalline site.
Consumes exactly these crystals/connections for the Dieudonné-crystal classification; CR.1 is declared the generic supplier, so the overlap is by design rather than duplication.

targets.target: RΓ_crys and relative Ru_* on the enhanced sheaf category
targets.note: Mathlib defines abelian sheaf cohomology on an arbitrary site as Ext from the constant sheaf, which is the generic carrier; but there is no crystalline site to apply it to and no higher direct image Ru_* along a morphism of sites.

targets.target: The linearization functor L(M) and its acyclicity for affine crystalline calculations
targets.note: Absent.

targets.target: PD Poincaré lemma: crystalline cohomology computed by the de Rham complex of the PD envelope of a smooth embedding, with coefficients in a crystal
targets.note: Absent, and both inputs are absent too: there is no PD envelope, and there is no algebraic de Rham complex Ω^•_{B/A} in either library — `grep -rl -i 'de rham'` over the two Lean trees hits only Mathlib/RingTheory/Perfectoid/BDeRham.lean (the period ring) and an unrelated parity file.

targets.target: Independence of the embedding via products, Čech–Alexander totalizations and explicit homotopies/refinement maps
targets.note: Generic Čech nerves and a Čech complex functor for sheaf cohomology exist; the Čech–Alexander complex of a crystalline embedding and its homotopies do not.

targets.target: For a smooth lift, identification of crystalline with de Rham cohomology and comparison of filtrations
targets.note: Absent (no crystalline cohomology and no de Rham cohomology of a scheme in either library).

targets.target: Formal p-adic version by derived inverse limit, compatible with the finite-level theory
targets.note: Absent; derived inverse limits of towers of complexes are not set up either (no `Rlim` for towers in the derived category, no derived completeness).

duplicates.note: Builds the derived-de-Rham-to-crystalline comparison map from polynomial resolutions, PD envelopes and this Poincaré lemma; DD.4 consumes CR.2 rather than reproving it, but the PD-envelope de Rham complex is shared.
Builds the absolute A_cris comparison 'by compatible PD envelopes and the all-coordinates construction' — the same PD-envelope de Rham computation in the A_inf setting.
Proves the log PD Poincaré lemma and its descent, i.e. the same theorem with a log structure.
Consumes CR.2 for the prismatic/crystalline comparison; the Čech–Alexander style independence-of-embedding argument recurs there for prisms.

targets.target: Crystalline descent for the chosen topology via site comparisons
targets.note: Generic descent/comparison-lemma machinery for sites exists in mathlib (dense subsites, descent data, IsStack); the crystalline instance does not.

targets.target: For proper smooth X/k with k perfect: a perfect W(k)-complex, finiteness of crystalline cohomology and compatible reductions
targets.note: W(k) is available as a complete DVR with its truncations W_n(k), so the coefficient ring and its reductions exist; the cohomology and its perfectness/finiteness do not. Note also that 'perfect complex' as a predicate is absent from mathlib (`grep -P 'PerfectComplex'` finds nothing).

targets.target: Derived base-change maps for crystalline families under flat/perfect coefficient hypotheses, with the cases where they are equivalences
targets.note: Absent.

targets.target: Künneth formula and cup products for crystalline cohomology in the proper smooth scope
targets.note: No Künneth theorem exists anywhere in the baseline (`grep -i -P '\t[^\t]*(Kunneth|Künneth)'` on declarations.tsv is empty), and the only cup products are in continuous/group cohomology in Tau Ceti, not in sheaf cohomology. The cited Tau Ceti file is the continuous-cohomology cup product (line number approximate; see the file for the exact declarations) and is only a structural analogue.

targets.target: Frobenius from the special-fibre morphism and its Witt/PD lift, with semilinear maps separated from their linearizations
targets.note: The Witt-vector Frobenius and its semilinear-equivalence form exist, together with the absolute Frobenius of a CharP ring; missing is the crystalline Frobenius on cohomology and the linearization of a semilinear map. Line for `frobenius` is nominal — it is in the CharP files, not in a crystalline context.

targets.target: Inverse-limit/finiteness argument following the Berthelot–Ogus Appendix B corrigendum, with a derived replacement for the termwise-surjective tower
targets.note: Absent; there is no derived-limit API for towers of complexes in either library, so neither the erroneous nor the corrected statement can be expressed.

duplicates.note: Split off from this layer's own text; it owns the rational-isogeny conclusion of the same Frobenius construction.
Split off from this layer; owns the trace/duality statement that this layer explicitly excludes.

Also carries the Berthelot–Ogus Appendix B corrigendum target ('the claimed projective replacement is an isomorphism in the derived category'), so the derived-tower replacement is stated in both layers.
Consumes the finiteness/base-change output; the proper smooth crystalline comparison there reuses the same perfect-W(k)-complex statement.

targets.target: Frobenius on crystalline cohomology as a rational isogeny (φ becomes an isomorphism after inverting p), proved through de Rham–Witt/Cartier control or the classical crystalline argument
targets.note: Absent: neither crystalline cohomology nor de Rham–Witt exists, so no isogeny statement can be formed.

targets.target: Finite-free F-crystals as a category distinct from torsion cohomology modules
targets.note: Mathlib has the φ-semilinear K(p,k)-vector-space notion and proves the one-dimensional Dieudonné–Manin classification over an algebraically closed k (slopes m ∈ ℤ). It is not an F-crystal: there is no integral W-lattice, no Frobenius-divisibility condition, and the layer itself says a bare semilinear vector space does not give one.

targets.target: Convergent versus overconvergent F-isocrystals kept distinct
targets.note: Neither notion exists; there is no convergence/overconvergence condition anywhere in the baseline.

duplicates.note: This substage is carved out of CR.3's own description text, which states the Frobenius construction and defers its isogeny conclusion here.
Supplies the de Rham–Witt/Cartier control through which this isogeny is to be proved; the slope/degree filtration targets overlap.
Consumes CR.3 and owns the convergent/overconvergent F-isocrystal theory that this substage is told not to conflate.
Develops the isocrystal/Banach–Colmez side and warns against circular use of the classification; the same Dieudonné–Manin material appears there.

targets.target: The proper smooth crystalline trace map and its normalization in top degree
targets.note: Absent; no trace map for any sheaf-cohomology theory exists in the baseline.

targets.target: Cup-product perfect pairing in the derived sense, with a derived dual rather than a perfect pairing on each group
targets.note: Absent. Mathlib has monoidal/dualizable-object machinery in the abstract (`CategoryTheory.Monoidal`), but no cup product on sheaf cohomology and no duality theorem.

targets.target: Compatibility with reduction, the Gysin formalism, the diagonal class and evaluation/coevaluation
targets.note: Absent; there is no Gysin map or diagonal class in either library.

targets.target: Projective-space normalization, functoriality and base change of the trace before CP.6 imports them
targets.note: Absent.

duplicates.note: Carved out of CR.3's text; CR.3 states explicitly that the trace/duality statement is this successor and not one of its own inputs.
Ekedahl's de Rham–Witt duality is named here as the complementary acquired route, so CR.4's de Rham–Witt complex is a shared input.
Owns proper support, traces and Poincaré duality for curves in the adic étale setting — a parallel trace/duality package for a different cohomology theory.
Owns the integral/analytic/diamond comparison of the six operations including duality; the trace-normalisation and diagonal-class formalism recurs there.

targets.target: Witt complexes W_nΩ^• with restriction R, Frobenius F, Verschiebung V, Teichmüller lift and dlog, and the full relation list
targets.note: The 'existing Witt-vector carrier' the layer plans to build on is genuinely there: W(R), W_n(R), F, V, Teichmüller, ghost components, FV = p, V F = p on char-p rings. The de Rham–Witt complex itself is absent — `grep -i -P '\t[^\t]*DeRhamWitt'` on declarations.tsv returns nothing in either library, and there is no differential-graded Witt object and no dlog.

targets.target: Universal property of Witt complexes, with the graded Frobenius distinguished from the degree-scaled crystalline Frobenius
targets.note: Absent.

targets.target: Polynomial basic Witt differentials, localization and étale descent of W_nΩ; ghost-coordinate inversion under torsion hypotheses
targets.note: Mathlib proves the ghost map is bijective exactly when p is invertible, which is the torsion hypothesis the layer wants respected; but there are no basic Witt differentials and no localization/étale-descent statement for a Witt complex.

targets.target: Agreement with the classical de Rham–Witt complex for smooth algebras over a perfect F_p-field
targets.note: Absent.

targets.target: The BLM model: strict saturated Dieudonné complexes, saturation, V-adic (Nygaard-style) completion, its universal property, and the fixed-point characterization of Lη_p
targets.note: Absent. No Dieudonné complex, no saturation functor, and no décalage/Lη operator anywhere in the baseline (that is AInfCohomology AI.1's target and is also absent).

targets.target: Relative Langer–Zink de Rham–Witt theory for smooth algebras over a base with p nilpotent, plus its relative crystalline comparison
targets.note: Absent.

targets.target: Finite-level and inverse-limit comparisons with CR.2, slope/degree filtrations and convergence of the associated spectral sequences
targets.note: Mathlib has an abstract spectral-sequence/spectral-object formalism with convergence statements, so the carrier exists; nothing about slopes, degrees or de Rham–Witt does.

duplicates.note: Owns the positive-degree q-de Rham–Witt complex and explicitly imports ordinary de Rham–Witt with its restriction maps from CR.4; the F/V relation lists overlap while the restriction-map question separates them.
Relative q-Witt rings and finite étale lifts duplicate the localization/étale-descent half of this layer in the q-deformed setting.

Uses CR.4's Langer–Zink objects for the relative de Rham–Witt comparison; the same universal Witt-complex maps appear on both sides.
Witt vectors and residue-characteristic calculations reuse the Witt-complex/de Rham–Witt package for K-theory computations.

targets.target: Prelog rings and the associated log structure on the étale site, with charts and groupification
targets.note: Groupification of a commutative monoid is available (monoid localization at the whole monoid), but there is no prelog ring, no log structure and no chart: `grep -i -P '\t[^\t]*(prelog|LogStructure|LogRing)'` on declarations.tsv is empty in both libraries.

targets.target: Integral, fine and saturated monoids, and the distinction between integrality and saturation
targets.note: Mathlib has the saturation of a submonoid of a group (elements with a power in the submonoid), which is the right notion of a saturated monoid once the monoid is embedded in its groupification; but there is no `IsIntegral`/`IsFine`/`IsSaturated` predicate on an abstract commutative monoid, and no finite-generation ('fine') package. Line 41 is nominal — check the file for the exact declaration names.
